patient_facts.text: Earlier this morning he fainted: he unexpectedly collapsed and lost consciousness.
patient_facts.quote: I fainted. / Earlier this morning, while carrying groceries to the car with my wife, I unexpectedly collapsed and lost consciousness.

patient_facts.text: He was carrying groceries to the car with his wife when it happened.
patient_facts.quote: while carrying groceries to the car with my wife

patient_facts.text: Thinks he lost consciousness first and then fell to the ground.
patient_facts.quote: I think I lost consciousness and then fell down on the ground.

patient_facts.text: His wife told him he did not respond to her for several minutes.
patient_facts.quote: My wife told me that I did not respond to her for several minutes.

patient_facts.text: His heart started racing just before he fell.
patient_facts.quote: Yes, just before I fell down, my heart started racing.

patient_facts.text: Noticed nothing out of the ordinary before he fell, such as sounds, odors, or lights.
Felt lightheaded right before the fall.
patient_facts.quote: I felt lightheaded right before the fall.

patient_facts.text: His wife said his arms and legs began to tremble after he collapsed and that this lasted about 30 seconds.
patient_facts.quote: Yes, my wife mentioned that my arms and legs began to tremble after I collapsed. / She indicated it lasted approximately 30 seconds.

patient_facts.text: Did not lose control of his bladder.
No confusion on waking up after the episode.
No similar falls, lightheadedness, or passing out in the past.
High blood pressure for the past 15 years.
patient_facts.quote: High blood pressure for the past 15 years

patient_facts.text: Had a heart attack 1 year ago.
Had his appendix removed (date not given).
Father died of a heart attack at age 55.
patient_facts.quote: My father died from a heart attack at age 55

patient_facts.text: Mother has died; he says she 'died in good health' (cause and age not given).

patient_facts.text: Drinks three to four beers a week.

patient_facts.quote: I had smoked a pack a day for the previous 25 years.

additional_considerations.rationale: Usually triggered by emotional stress or pain and heralded by nausea, sweating, pallor and feeling faint.
His antihypertensives raise the risk, but this syncope is usually postural and his orthostatic vital signs were normal.
Mechanical causes (also HOCM, atrial myxoma) are usually exertional and without warning; no murmur or other supporting findings.

source_issues: Opening scenario says he complains 'of pulling out a few hours earlier', evidently a corruption of 'passing out'.
Name inconsistency: the opening scenario and sample closure say Keller; two doctor questions (cc, p013) say 'Mr. Kella'.

e008 'Babinski sign present bilaterally' does not state the plantar response direction in standard terms and a bilateral positive Babinski conflicts with the otherwise normal neurological exam and the gold (no exam findings). Kept neutral as recorded (x020); not converted to positive or negative.
p026 'my mother died in good health' is odd (possibly a corruption of 'is alive and in good health'); recorded literally with a flag. The note FH mentions only the father.
The note SH says 'Drinks 34 beers/week', an OCR artifact for the script's 'three to four beers a week'.
Gold rank-2 history finding 'Taking a P-blocker (atenolol)' has an OCR artifact for β-blocker; cleaned in gold.
p020 repeats the weakness/numbness question from p011; both ids are attached to the same facts.
The raw checklist contains a stray '581'; not patient content.
annotator_notes: Event facts about this morning's episode (collapse, palpitations, lightheadedness, shaking, no tongue biting or incontinence, no confusion afterwards) are historical; current ROS denials are current.
p007 and p008 are merged so the 30-second duration stays with the shaking (rule 4).
Both the shaking and the duration of unresponsiveness are reported second-hand from his wife, and the texts say so.
The orthostatic finding in e002 is recorded as a separate vital-sign record (v006).
'Married with three children' from the raw Patient Description is kept as an acting note; the SP notes themselves are 'None.'
Reviewer edit: x020 restored to the source wording ("present"); the doubt is kept as a flag on the record instead of in the finding text.
